subject: Indemnity redlines — privilege & evidence preservation; proposed runbook (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Anna Ross <anna.ross@acmecorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — indemnity clarifications and evidence protocol

Olga,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our outside counsel reviewed the MSA + Order Form and pushed back on a few indemnity points that will block procurement signoff unless clarified: primarily (1) defend vs reimburse language for third-party copyright/patent claims tied to model outputs, (2) the scope for claims where customer data was used to fine-tune models, and (3) evidence preservation — how Redwood will provide logs, samples, and a redacted evidence set while preserving privilege.

Two asks to keep this moving: can you (a) confirm whether Redwood is willing to adopt a 30-day notice window and (b) provide a short runbook describing the evidence-handling process (where evidence lives, how we’ll redact privileged material, S3 access vs. secure share, point people and SLA for evidence production)? Procurement says they need these on record to complete the risk assessment.

I’ve attached our standard indemnity checklist so you can map items back to the contract. Happy to hop on a quick call later today if that’s helpful.

— Anna
Anna Ross
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
anna.ross@acmecorp.com

Attachment: ACME_Indemnity_Checklist.pdf (attachment referenced; not included)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Anna Ross <anna.ross@acmecorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — indemnity clarifications and evidence protocol

Anna — thanks for the clear note and the checklist. Appreciate the visibility into procurement’s gating items.

High-level answers up front:
- Notice window: we are prepared to codify a 30-day notice window for most third-party IP claims; exceptions (urgent regulatory takedown subpoenas) will be handled on an expedited incident basis and are covered by our incident escalation policy.
- Evidence runbook: see draft below. I’ll attach a template evidence manifest (for your counsel) and a proposed redline of the indemnity paragraph that reflects our pragmatic defend-or-reimburse compromise.

Draft evidence-handling runbook (summary):
1) Initial triage (0–48 hrs): customer provides formal notice via indemnity@redwood.com and fills the evidence manifest. We acknowledge within 4 business hours.
2) Preservation (48–72 hrs): SRE snapshots (token logs, request/response samples) are captured to a legal hold S3 bucket with restricted access. We create an evidence manifest (CSV) listing sample ids, timestamps, and redaction flags.
3) Privilege/redaction: legal (internal counsel) pre-screens artifacts; privileged communications and internal notes are redacted before export. We will provide a redaction summary and privilege log.
4) Access & delivery: delivery via secure share link (time-limited, IP-restricted) or by secure S3 role-assignment; if Acme requires direct S3 access we can support a cross-account read-only IAM role for a defined 30-day window.
5) SLA & escalation: evidence production target is 10 business days for the initial package; critical items (samples needed for injunction hearings) within 72 hours with senior counsel escalation.

Open question for procurement: will Acme accept redacted sample sets as part of the initial package, with an option for privileged-invoked re-review in camera if a court requires unredacted material?

Kimberly — can you take this draft and propose contract language for (a) a 30-day notice window, (b) a limited S3 cross-account access option, and (c) a clause about privilege-protected evidence and privilege logs? Jordan — I’m copying you for visibility on the operational steps and to flag any constraints (SRE support, on-call coverage).

Thanks — I’ll stand by for a short call if that helps move this along.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachment: evidence_manifest_template.xlsx
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, Anna Ross <anna.ross@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — indemnity clarifications and evidence protocol

All — I reviewed Olga’s runbook and mapped proposed contract language below. I also attached a marked redline (ACME_MSA_Indemnity_Redline.docx) and a short commentary PDF. Key legal positions:

1) Scope carving — training data: Redwood will defend and indemnify against third-party IP claims arising from use of Redwood’s base models or Redwood-provided fine-tuning datasets. Redwood will not accept indemnity obligations for customer-supplied proprietary training data unless the parties explicitly confirm in the Order Form that the dataset has been provided under warranties of ownership and non-infringement. Proposed clause: "Customer data carveout: indemnity obligations for claims related to customer-supplied data require a separate warranty and data provenance appendix attached to the Order Form."

2) Defend v. reimburse: we propose an optional defend-or-reimburse ladder: Redwood will (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to defend at our expense for covered claims; if Redwood declines defense for reasons listed in the clause (e.g., conflict of interest, material breach by Customer), Redwood will reimburse Customer’s reasonable costs of defense up to the cap.

3) Privilege / evidence production: add an evidence-preservation clause specifying Redwood’s production processes, privilege log requirements, and a mutual-in-camera review process for contested privilege redactions. Also add limits on scope: Redwood’s obligation is limited to logs and sample outputs reasonably necessary to litigate the claim (not wholesale model weights or internal training corpora).

4) Notice & mitigation: 30-day notice, with a 72-hour escalation path for injunctive matters. Include a cooperation covenant (reasonable cooperation) with defined windows.

5) Cap and insurance offset: propose a cap tied to Order Form value (e.g., aggregate cap = 3x annual committed spend) and standard carveouts for willful misconduct.

I’ve flagged suggested edits inline in ACME_MSA_Indemnity_Redline.docx. Anna — the tractable asks are (i) whether Acme can represent in the Order Form that any customer-supplied training datasets include a provenance statement and (ii) whether your procurement/legal team can accept redacted evidence subject to in-camera review for privileged materials. If you’re open to those two, we can move to a short counterproposal and submit to procurement.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Kim / Olga — thanks for the clear, practical approach. A few quick reactions from Acme legal / procurement:

- Training data carveout: acceptable in principle if Acme can provide the provenance statement. We will add a line to the Order Form data appendix confirming provenance & ownership where relevant.
- Redacted evidence: must be accompanied by a privilege log and vendor certification we did not withhold any non-privileged material. The in-camera option works for judge-ordered disclosures.
- Cap: procurement will not accept a cap less than 2x ARR for strategic, high-value contracts; we are prepared to discuss insurance-first waterfalls and allocation to reach middle ground.
- DocuSign: I’m attaching our procurement-approved signature packet for the MSA + Order Form and a short list of priority items we need cleared in the next pass. Please review and we can aim to exchange a clean counter by Mon EOD. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/some-ds-link/0a1b2c3d

We’ll also set a 30-minute slot Monday to finalize open terms; procurement will invite our outside counsel and the ACME technical counsel who will need to validate the evidence manifest format.

Best,
— Anna
